run.question:
Customers reported slow checkout for the last hour. Check our Datadog APM
traces for the checkout-service and find which downstream call is slow.

report.summary: The requested Datadog APM traces are not available in this Run: the only trace/metric backends configured are Jaeger and Prometheus on target m0-otel-20260909, and every trace call (traces_list_services, traces_list_operations, traces_search) and every Prometheus call (get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target, list_prometheus_rules) returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no per-call latency could be read for checkout or for any downstream. Elasticsearch holds no indices at all (elasticsearch_list_indices on "*" returned zero indices, elasticsearch_search on "*" matched no index). What could be observed is Kubernetes state and application logs only, and neither shows a slow dependency: checkout and its dependencies (cart, currency, email, payment, product-catalog, shipping, valkey-cart) each report 1/1 ready/available replicas, and the retained checkout logs show the payment leg completing ~15-23 ms after the PlaceOrder line in every sampled order, which is counter-evidence against payment being the slow call (limited to that one leg). No fault-injection flag is enabled in the flagd-config ConfigMap (all defaultVariant values are "off"), so no flag-based latency injection was observed for checkout or its dependencies. The checkout container did restart during the window (previous instance terminated 08:04:13Z, exit 255, reason Unknown; new instance started 08:04:20Z) and cluster events show bulk pod SandboxChanged/Started activity in otel-demo at the same time, but no evidence ties that restart to slow checkout, and its trigger is unknown. The specific downstream call that is slow therefore remains unidentified; no root cause is named.

claims.text: Deployments checkout, cart, currency, email, payment, product-catalog, shipping and valkey-cart in namespace otel-demo each report replicas=1, readyReplicas=1, availableReplicas=1 and observedGeneration matching generation (all 1) at query time.

Pod checkout-6578865d87-5zx6n (namespace otel-demo, image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-checkout, owner ReplicaSet checkout-6578865d87) is Running and ready; its current checkout container started at 2026-11-22T08:04:20Z, restartCount is 2, and the previous instance terminated at 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z with exitCode 255 and reason Unknown.

Cluster events in the authorized window include 22 Pod SandboxChanged, 23 Pod Created, 23 Pod Pulled and 23 Pod Started events for involvedObject.namespace otel-demo, plus 5 Pod Unhealthy and 1 Pod BackOff in otel-demo, i.e. a bulk pod restart wave across that namespace around the same time as the checkout container restart.

The retained checkout application logs (100 newest of 188 lines, 2026-11-22T08:23:54Z to 08:44:57Z) show repeated info-level sequences "[PlaceOrder] user_id=..." then "payment went through (transaction_id: ...)" then "order confirmation email sent to ..."; e.g. PlaceOrder at 08:26:16.174Z and payment went through at 08:26:16.197Z (~23 ms), and PlaceOrder at 08:42:00.260Z and payment at 08:42:00.282Z (~22 ms).

ConfigMap flagd-config in namespace otel-demo contains demo.flagd.json in which every declared flag has defaultVariant "off": productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad.

In the sampled checkout order flow the payment step completed about 15-23 ms after the PlaceOrder log line in every observed order, so the retained logs do not support payment as the slow downstream call; this covers only the payment leg (not cart, currency, shipping, product-catalog or email timings) and only the log lines retained from 08:23:54Z onward.

A feature-flag-driven latency injection (e.g. imageSlowLoad 5sec/10sec, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable) was considered as the cause of slow checkout; the flagd-config ConfigMap read shows all defaultVariant values set to "off", so no such fault was observed enabled.

The slow downstream call could be any of checkout's dependencies (cart/valkey-cart, currency, shipping, product-catalog, email, payment) and cannot be narrowed from the evidence available in this Run; a per-call (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds by rpc_service/rpc_method) comparison against a pre-incident baseline is what would identify it.

The checkout container restart at 2026-11-22T08:04:20Z and the namespace-wide pod SandboxChanged/Started wave are a mechanism (node/host-level restart) rather than the cause of the reported slow checkout; no checkout latency or error signal was observed around it in the available logs.

gaps: Datadog APM is not a configured data source in this Run (available sources are Jaeger, Prometheus, Kubernetes, Elasticsearch), so the traces the question asks for could not be queried at all; which downstream call is slow is therefore not answered from Datadog data.

The Jaeger trace backend on target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for traces_list_services, traces_list_operations and traces_search in the query window 2026-11-22T07:45:02Z-08:45:02Z; no span, span duration or parent-child call edge for checkout was obtainable.

Prometheus on target m0-otel-20260909 returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE for get_label_values, get_metric_names, execute_prometheus_instant_query, metrics_range_query, get_prometheus_target and list_prometheus_rules; latency series such as rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and traces_span_metrics_calls_total could not be read, and per-call latency of checkout's downstreams is unknown, not zero.
No latency baseline exists for checkout or any downstream, so no latency trend can be asserted in either direction.

Elasticsearch has no indices: elasticsearch_list_indices with pattern "*" returned 0 indices and elasticsearch_search with index "*" reported no matching index, so no log store outside Kubernetes pod logs was available.
A checkout log query filtered on err|error|fail|timeout|deadline|unavailable returned no matching lines (status no_data); a non-match is not proof that no such line was written.

Checkout log retention in the fetched view begins at 2026-11-22T08:23:54Z, so the first ~39 minutes of the authorized window are not covered by those logs, and no previous-container log lines were read (0 lines for the previous instance).

The trigger of the checkout container restart (previous instance exit code 255, reason Unknown, finished 2026-11-22T08:04:13Z) and of the bulk otel-demo pod SandboxChanged wave is unknown; no evidence links it to slow checkout.
Unnamed per-pod application timings for cart, currency, shipping, product-catalog and email were not measurable: their pods were only checked for replica readiness, and their logs were not read.
next_steps: Restore or point at a reachable trace backend (Jaeger target m0-otel-20260909 currently returns SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) or enable the Datadog APM integration, then compare checkout client-span durations by rpc_service/rpc_method (rpc_client_duration_milliseconds) across the incident hour against a pre-incident baseline.
Once Prometheus is reachable, query traces_span_metrics_calls_total and rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count filtered on service_name="checkout" to rank downstream calls by latency and error rate.
If traces stay unavailable, read the application logs of cart, currency, shipping, product-catalog and email pods for the same window to look for slow-request or timeout lines.
Confirm the cause and scope of the 2026-11-22T08:04Z pod restart wave (node or host event) before attributing any customer-visible impact to it.

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.

Only what the containers wrote to standard output and standard error and the node still keeps: the current instance and the one before it, nothing older and nothing from a pod that no longer exists. No matching line is not proof that something did not happen; lines cut by limit or by the read limit, and lines not read, are unknown, not absent.
